rea.capabilityFinding: REA JavaScript/Electron analysis is appropriate for authorized local application artifacts; it is not a universal URL/repository auditor. Use source inspection, official docs and tests for Rust projects, protocol docs and API services.
rea.limitations: Prior local analysis is structural evidence only; no claim of runtime loading, semantic equivalence, upstream behavior, provider correctness, or economic advantage.

discoveries: Upstream exposes streams for slots, blocks, transactions, deshred transactions and account updates; the protocol surface is broader than a logs-only transaction feed.

The upstream changelog records replay reconnect edge cases involving duplicate events, partial slots and fork/blockhash verification. Recovery should therefore preserve slot sealing, block identity, replay/live-tail deduplication and explicit equivocation checks.
Current upstream also documents TLS/auth listener configuration and known block reconstruction limitations; availability of a stream does not establish complete canonical block evidence.
patterns: pin protocol/client versions and test supported update variants
sources.overlap: SYLPH already uses the Triton Yellowstone Node package, retains raw protobuf bytes in a captured deserializer, and routes versioned observations into canonical ingress. The current dependency is @triton-one/yellowstone-grpc 4.0.2; compatibility against current upstream protocol/replay behavior is not established by this review.
risks: upstream client and server versions may diverge
replay payloads may duplicate or conflict across providers/forks
transport freshness must not be substituted for finalized completeness
validation: pin server/client/proto versions
fixture partial-slot replay, duplicate updates, reconnect equivocation and live-tail handoff
compare finalized slot/blockhash/transaction sets independently
test bounded backpressure and restart recovery

discoveries: REA documents local analysis workflows for JavaScript/Electron apps and native/managed targets, with evidence and limitations attached to findings.
The tool is scoped to supported application artifacts and approved observations; it does not turn arbitrary remote websites or a 288-link catalog into verified integrations.
Existing local REA output is structural evidence for SYLPH emitted JavaScript. It cannot prove runtime module identity, source semantics, service behavior or profitability.
patterns: use REA only on an appropriate authorized target
pair structural mappings with deterministic runtime tests
sources.overlap: Prior local runs analyzed fresh Engine and Terminal artifacts. This batch did not run a new REA command; repo environment discovery did not find a standalone rea executable on PATH.
risks: optional toolchain/Windows limitations may make some REA workflows unavailable
static mapping can be mistaken for proof of execution
remote third-party targets require separate authorization and appropriate tool support
validation: record pinned REA version and exact command/target for each run
retain raw output and hash
use deterministic regression tests for behavior claims
keep REA outside runtime and all trading decisions

provenance: Local SYLPH Jito status adapters and live-status report
discoveries: A successful sendBundle response with bundle_id means receipt, not landing; the documented status method must be used to observe bundle processing.
Jito bundles are atomic and all-or-nothing within a slot, while tip amount participates in an auction and a low tip may fail selection.
Jito recommends simulation and cost/latency-aware tip selection; transport connectivity and tip-floor reads alone do not verify landed transactions or realized costs.
patterns: separate submission receipt from landing/finalization evidence
correlate bundle IDs to transaction signatures and settlement
measure tip, priority fees, base fees, retries and failed/uncled outcomes
sources.overlap: SYLPH has read-only Block Engine connectivity and tip-floor research projections. Existing live status explicitly labels them CONNECTIVITY_ONLY / tip data; bundle submission and realized landed-cost telemetry remain unverified.
risks: false success if receipt is shown as landing
tips and priority fees can exceed expected edge
bundle execution differs from ordinary transaction submission
validation: only in isolated fixtures or explicitly authorized non-capital environment
test receipt-without-landing and status timeout
reconcile bundle status, signature, finalized transaction and wallet deltas
record all fees and tips against realized outcomes

provenance: Official Jupiter Developer docs and Swap V2 API reference
Local Jupiter research adapter and project integration notes
discoveries: The current V2 API reference exposes an /order endpoint that returns an assembled transaction and identifies taker as a required request field; an order response is not merely a quote payload.

SYLPH's existing Jupiter research adapter calls /swap/v2/order, rate-limits requests, validates returned amounts, discards unsigned transaction data, and marks results QUOTE_ONLY with executionAuthorized false.

Local integration notes say authenticated V2 use requires configured API key and taker public key; neither setting was present in the captured environment, so this authenticated contract was not exercised.
patterns: keep quote-only response schemas distinct from prepared transaction schemas
record quote timestamps and sequential round-trip window
discard transaction payload in research-only adapter
sources.overlap: A read-only Jupiter adapter exists, but it does not submit or sign. Existing audit reports measured quotes that are snapshots rather than fills or profit estimates.
risks: /order may return transaction material even for a quote workflow
sequential quotes span time and market state
fees, landing probability, price movement and failed execution are excluded
API key/taker contract not verified in this environment
validation: recheck official V2 schema/version before updates
fixture authenticated and unauthenticated cases, error/oversize responses, token decimals and partial quotes
never pass an assembled payload from research to signer
compare quotes with confirmed fills only in authorized paper/sandbox workflows

provenance: Official Pump public documentation repository README
discoveries: Official docs describe new Pump curve v3 and PumpSwap v2 instruction families, multi-hop swaps, pump-token quote mints and fee sweeps; the lifecycle is broader than a SOL-only bonding curve followed by one AMM.

PumpSwap effective quote reserves are the quote-vault balance plus signed virtual_quote_reserves; docs explicitly warn the signed reserve may be negative and raw vault balance alone is not the quote reserve.
Fees can accrue on curves/pools and be swept separately; synthetic migration behavior and creator/holder-reward fee variants affect interpretation of trade events and quote/accounting state.
patterns: model quote mint and reserve signs explicitly
separate trade events from fee-sweep events
bind pool/lifecycle state to slot and canonical account identity
sources.overlap: SYLPH's Pump adapter is a read-only bonding-curve account reader and explicitly does not return a swap quote. It accepts both SPL Token and Token-2022 mint owners and retains raw reserve values. Graduated-venue fixed-reserve assumptions are separately identified in existing research notes and need a protocol/math review before any economic-semantic patch.
risks: signed reserve coercion or raw-vault pricing can misquote
curve completion is not proof of destination-pool liquidity
fee sweeps and migration events can corrupt volume/PnL attribution if treated as trades
validation: pin official IDL and SDK versions
differentially decode versioned raw transactions/account fixtures
add signed i128, non-SOL quote mint, fee accrual/sweep and synthetic-migration fixtures
derive post-migration executable quotes from verified pool state and test sell-side feasibility
